import re
p='index.html'; s=open(p).read()
for i in range(2,9):
    s=s.replace(f'class="sched-day" style="grid-column:{i}"', f'class="sched-day d{i}"')
    s=s.replace(f'class="sched-day today" style="grid-column:{i}"', f'class="sched-day today d{i}"')
s=s.replace('class="customers-label" style="font-weight:400;letter-spacing:0"','class="customers-label"')
s=s.replace('class="avatar" style="background:var(--p-ana)"','class="avatar av-ana"')
s=s.replace('class="avatar" style="background:var(--p-jonah)"','class="avatar av-jonah"')
s=s.replace('class="avatar" style="background:var(--p-mei)"','class="avatar av-mei"')
s=s.replace('<ul class="policy esc-list" style="margin-top:0">','<ul class="policy">')
css_add='''.d2 { grid-column: 2; } .d3 { grid-column: 3; } .d4 { grid-column: 4; } .d5 { grid-column: 5; }
.d6 { grid-column: 6; } .d7 { grid-column: 7; } .d8 { grid-column: 8; }
'''
s=s.replace('.sched-corner {', css_add+'.sched-corner {',1)
s=s.replace('.customers-label { font-size: 0.875rem;','.customers-label { font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0; font-size: 0.875rem;')
s=s.replace('.avatar { ','.av-ana { background: var(--p-ana); } .av-jonah { background: var(--p-jonah); } .av-mei { background: var(--p-mei); }\n.avatar { ',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print(s.count('style="'))
EOF
grep -n 'style="' index.html | head

content.text:
I've written `index.html` to the working directory. It's a single file with all the HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline, and the only external requests are IBM Plex fonts from Google Fonts. I checked it in headless Chrome at 1440px and 390px: every section renders, there's no horizontal scrolling at 390px, and all the interactive parts work.

**Look and feel.** I went for a duty-roster-on-paper style rather than the usual SaaS template: a warm off-white background, dark green-black text, and one orange accent (the pager color). Times and incident IDs are in a monospace font, sections are separated by thin rules instead of heavy cards, and there are no gradients or purple.

**What's on the page:**
- **Header:** sticky. At 900px and below the nav links move into a menu button, and "Start free trial" stays visible. Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the button. If JavaScript is off, the menu links are just shown, so navigation still works.
- **Hero illustration:** built in HTML/CSS as a week view of an on-call schedule for a "payments-api" service.
  - It shows primary, secondary and team-lead shifts, a "now" line and an approved swap on Saturday.
  - It also has a fairness strip with hours per person, a handoff card with two open incidents carried over, and an alert acknowledged in 3 minutes.
  - On a phone, names in the schedule switch to initials so the 7-day grid still fits.
  - Screen readers get a single text description of the whole picture.
- **Pricing toggle:** two radio buttons, so arrow keys work. Annual shows $7 and $13, plus "Billed annually, $84 / $156 per user per year". Screen readers hear when the prices change. Team has a "Most popular" badge.
- **FAQ:** built on the browser's native expand/collapse element, so it works with the keyboard and without JavaScript.
- **Signup form:** has a visible "Work email" label. An empty or badly formatted email shows an inline error. A valid one shows a short "Starting trial…" state and then a confirmation message. There's no backend, so that submission is simulated.

**Copy I added beyond your brief:**
- Section headings, plan descriptions and the five FAQ answers.
- A footnote under the results explaining how the figures were measured (made up, like the rest of the content).
- A "Save up to 22%" label on the annual option. 22% is the Team saving; Business saves about 19%.
- Two things I invented that you may want to cut: an "All systems operational" line in the footer, and FAQ answers that promise no per-message SMS fees and an automatic drop to Free when the trial ends.

All buttons and links are reachable with the keyboard and show a visible focus outline, and animations are switched off for people who set "reduce motion" in their system settings.
